div.div:
Gang Scheduling (All-or-Nothing)
Standard Kubernetes schedules pods one by one.
In distributed ML training (like PyTorch or TensorFlow), you might have 8 workers that must start at the exact same time to perform a "Collective Communication" (All-Reduce) operation.
The Problem: If a cluster has room for 6 pods, a standard scheduler will start those 6 and leave the last 2 "Pending." The first 6 will sit idle, consuming expensive GPU time while waiting for resources that may never come.
The Custom Solution: A custom scheduler uses Gang Scheduling. It won't start any pods unless the cluster has enough room for the entire training job.

div.div:
Standard Method: You can’t force the scheduler to do an "All-or-Nothing" start.
The "Workaround": You manually calculate your cluster size. If you have 8 workers, you ensure your cluster has exactly 8 (or more) GPU slots available before you hit kubectl apply.
The Failure Point: In a shared cluster, if a coworker submits a small 1-GPU pod 1 second before you, they might "steal" one of your slots. Your job starts with 7 workers, hangs, and you waste money. Standard K8s has no way to say "Hold these 7 slots until the 8th is free."
